❯ Write a 1500 word essay about the history of terminal emulators. Do not use any tools.

⏺ The Glass Teletype: A History of Terminal Emulators

Every time a developer opens a terminal window on a laptop, they are running a program that pretends to be a piece of
hardware that has not been manufactured in decades. The blinking cursor, the fixed-width grid of characters, the
escape sequences that change colors and move the cursor around: all of these are echoes of physical machines that once
sat on desks, humming and clattering, wired to mainframes and minicomputers in distant rooms. The terminal emulator
is one of the most durable pieces of software in computing history, and its story is a story of layered compatibility,
where each generation preserves the quirks of the last.

Before the screen

The ancestor of the terminal was the teleprinter, or teletype. Machines like the Teletype Model 33, introduced in
1963, were electromechanical typewriters that could send and receive characters over a serial line. They printed on
continuous paper, one
